parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Section four. You will hear a part of lecture about history of extreme sport. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Extreme sports are non-traditional sports and activities that require participants to combine athletic skill with pronounced risk. It is difficult to determine exactly when the term extremely sports came to refer to certain modern sports. While many extreme sports such as deep diving and surfing have usually been part of human history, so many extreme sports are often called lifestyle sports. They often involve speed, height, physical commitment. The practice of extreme sports can involve some risks, injuries, and even death if the athlete made a serious mistake. Technological advances have brought more reliable equipment, which making various sports a safer activity. The worldwide spread of extreme sports is attributed to the media. Televisions and the movies have been responsible for gaining a widespread participation in extreme sports.

In the nineteenth century, the acceptance by workforce extended. For those men with a lower leisure preference, Sundays were generally free from labor. One extreme sport was started by workers from a company in its free time. Employers commonly believe this leisure activity increased the productivity, and most importantly, increased workers' loyalty to the company.

The nineteenth century is considered by many to be the period when the truly modern game emerged. The changes that primarily spawned this modernization were to be the equipment of the game. Other sports such as golf was popularized and regularly attended by upper classes and nobility. Early golf clubs were made of materials similar to today's club, wood and iron. However, the biggest difference between the old golf clubs and modern ones was the use.

In the twentieth century, you may be wondering, what is it that attracts people to extreme sports in comparison to many traditional sports like football or basketball? One of the few things that coaches, players, and fans of nearly every competitive team sports seem to agree on these days is that there are too many regulations for these games. Secondly, most of the people involved in extreme sports do not feel the need for constant training and physical conditioning of their body. This leads to the stage where people love extreme sports do not take part in those games as they grow old.

Finally, participants described how extreme sports experiencing, controlling, and overcome fear made them positively change everyday life. A mountain climber described dealing with fear as empowering and feeling very at peace afterwards.

A base jumper described the pursuit as ultimate metaphor for jumping into the life rather than standing on the edge quivering.

In assessing the use of taxpayers' funds in bidding for major event or building a new stadium, or even trying to secure a new license for sports team, young sports participants clearly want government to put their emphasis on entertainment sports. Everyone can participate, everyone will have fun, and everyone can be involved. Individual competition, limitations, requirements, and other concerns simply aren't part of the equation. Young people dealt with self-existence to find authorities which are responsible for sport.

Combating racism in sport falls to everyone, including public authorities. Young people's responses to the changing world and their unique way is building their own community. Extreme sports are huge craze today. The psychology behind its popularity seems to be human nature to take risk for thrill, and the adventure continues to attract masses.

That is the end of part four. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to part four.

analyses.content: 录音中直接提到极限运动经常被称为“lifestyle” sports，这直接对应了题目中的also known as。
你可能会听到deep diving或surfing，但这只是录音中的举例，题目问的是这些运动的别称，请紧抓“often called”后面的关键信息。
While many extreme sports such as deep diving and surfing have usually been part of human history, so many extreme sports are often called lifestyle sports.
录音中说明了技术进步带来了更可靠的“equipment”，从而使各项运动变得更安全。
你可能只关注了大方向的technological advances，但填空需要的是具体的名词，真正使运动更安全的核心事物是装备。
Technological advances have brought more reliable equipment, which making various sports a safer activity.
录音明确指出一项极限运动是由一家公司的“workers”发起的，并且增加了对公司的忠诚度。
你可能会误听到下一句的employers（雇主），但录音清楚表达了雇主认为这项活动增加了工人的忠诚度，发起者和忠诚度的主体都是工人。

One extreme sport was started by workers from a company in its free time. Employers commonly believe this leisure activity increased the productivity, and most importantly, increased workers' loyalty to the company.
录音中提到像“golf”这样的其他运动在上层阶级中普及，这里的upper classes完美同义替换了题干的higher social class。
题目问的是被创造出来的具体运动像什么一样，你可能只听到了阶级名词而忽略了前面“such as”引导的举例名词“golf”。
Other sports such as golf was popularized and regularly attended by upper classes and nobility.
录音中提到人们将极限运动与足球、篮球等“traditional” sports进行了直接对比。
题目括号里已经举例了篮球，正好对应原文的like football or basketball，所以不要盲目填入具体的球类名称，要填它们前面的统称。
In the twentieth century, you may be wondering what is it that attracts people to extreme sports in comparison to many traditional sports like football or basketball.
录音指出大家一致认为团队运动有太多的“regulations”，完全对应题干的there are too many。
这句话的主语非常长，你可能会被教练、球员等一连串词汇干扰而跟丢，只需耐心听并死死抓住“too many”后面的核心名词即可。
One of the few things that coaches, players, and fans of nearly every competitive team sports seem to agree on these days is that there are too many regulations for these games.
录音提到参与极限运动的人不认为需要持续的“training”，原文的constant完美替换了题干要求的regular。
录音里紧接着出现了physical conditioning，但题目只需填一个词，最直接紧跟在修饰词后面的核心词就是训练。
Secondly, most of the people involved in extreme sports do not feel the need for constant training and physical conditioning of their body.
录音中提到参与者描述极限运动帮助他们克服和处理“fear”，这里的overcome和dealing with直接替换了题干的confront。
你可能会听到experiencing或controlling等并列的动词而分心，但只要听到克服（overcome），就能直接锁定它后面的宾语是恐惧。

Finally, participants described how extreme sports experiencing, controlling, and overcome fear made them positively change everyday life. A mountain climber described dealing with fear as empowering and feeling very at peace afterwards.
录音明确指出年轻的运动参与者希望政府将重点放在“entertainment” sports上，并在后续排除了个人竞争。
前面铺垫很长，有很多干扰词（如stadium, license等），你需要保持耐心，等到“want government to put their emphasis on”引出的核心诉求。

In assessing the use of taxpayers' funds in bidding for major event or building a new stadium or even trying to secure a new license for sports team, young sports participants clearly want government to put their emphasis on entertainment sports. Everyone can participate, everyone will have fun, and everyone can be involved. Individual competition, limitations, requirements, and other concerns simply aren't part of the equation.
录音提到年轻人应对不断变化的世界的独特方式是建立他们自己的“community”，这替换了题干中对新世界的态度和形成什么的内容。
如果你没有听出“对变化世界的反应”就是题目中“对新世界的态度”这层同义替换，就很容易在听力中错过紧跟着的答案词。
Young people's responses to the changing world and their unique way is building their own community.
